acceptanceCriteria: Runtime renders as a multi-ring structure (at minimum an outer boundary ring, a verification ring, and a core, evidence flowing through a ring distinct from the outer boundary) and during a Verify sequence the rings visibly activate in order rather than the whole shape being a single static inert form.

Flow connectors between architecture elements are curved data channels rendered with a Bezier or CatmullRom curve, not straight line segments, with multiple packets able to travel along an active curve.

The Work Item envelope renders as a boundary field using corner or edge markers implying a volume rather than a fully six-sided solid glass box, and has a distinct red blocked-boundary visual state available for an out-of-scope action.

Verification mode and the guided tour's verification scene play a deliberate cinematic sequence -- other elements dim, the camera pushes in slightly, GREEN transitions toward a blocked connector and Human Decision PENDING over roughly half a second to one second -- landing on the existing Verified not equal Approved line, and prefers-reduced-motion still collapses this to an immediate, non-animated state change.

Selective bloom (via @react-three/postprocessing) highlights only semantically active elements -- active evidence, the Runtime's currently-active ring, active flow packets, a blocked boundary, a selected Knowledge node -- while inactive elements remain matte, and the effect does not run as a full-scene always-on glow.

Knowledge shows a brief pulse and a new node appearing when a Work Item's archive stage transition occurs, and Trace gains an optional click-to-reveal 3D light-trail view that stays hidden until explicitly opened, with the existing UI timeline remaining the default/primary Trace interface.

The Human-Computer Interaction element's primary picker and heading label reads Human Control (en) / 人による制御 (ja) / 人工控制 (zh), while the WHAT detail text still names Human-Computer Interaction and the Define, Understand, Decide channels; the internal architecture id humanControlInterface is unchanged.

npm ci, lint, typecheck, unit tests, Playwright e2e, and the static export build all succeed with no regression to camera stability, three-mode navigation, i18n coverage, the restrained default Overview screen, or any prior WI's established acceptance behavior; performance stays reasonable -- bloom and curved-flow rendering do not turn the idle scene into a continuous full-frame-rate drain beyond what the active pulses already require.
goal: Ship v0.3 Spatial Identity: exactly five upgrades, no new architecture capabilities, no new tabs, no tour expansion, no new body text. (1) Runtime becomes a multi-ring Governance Engine (outer boundary ring, verification ring, evidence ring, core) that visibly sequences ring-by-ring during a Verify moment instead of sitting as an inert torus+icosahedron. (2) Flow connectors become curved data channels (Bezier/CatmullRom curves) with multiple packets traveling along the curve, replacing straight FlowLine segments. (3) The Work Item envelope becomes a boundary field (corner/edge markers implying a volume) instead of a full six-sided glass box, with a red boundary-block visual when execution would cross scope. (4) Verification gets a genuine cinematic beat: other scene elements dim, camera pushes in slightly, and GREEN -> (blocked X) -> Human Decision PENDING plays as a deliberate ~0.5-1s sequence, landing on the existing 'Verified != Approved' line. (5) Selective bloom via @react-three/postprocessing is added, applied only to semantically active elements (active evidence, the Runtime's active ring, active flow packets, a blocked boundary, a selected Knowledge node) -- inactive elements stay matte, this is not a full-scene glow. Three smaller companion fixes ride along: Knowledge gains a small pulse + new node animation when a Work Item archives into it; Trace gains an optional, click-to-reveal 3D light-trail representation (hidden by default, the existing UI timeline remains the primary interface); and the Human-Computer Interaction element's primary display label changes to the more intuitive 'Human Control' (en) / '人による制御' (ja) / '人工控制' (zh) in the picker/heading, while the fuller 'Human-Computer Interaction, Define -> Understand -> Decide' framing moves into the WHAT detail text -- the internal id humanControlInterface is unchanged.
intent: The Explorer's information architecture, Work Item semantics, Knowledge/Traceability, i18n, and camera stability all now pass user acceptance -- a non-programmer who knows the software dev process can understand what AI Cockpit does. But the 3D visual identity still reads as a competent generic React Three Fiber demo, not as something instantly recognizable as AI Cockpit specifically.
outOfScope: new body copy beyond what these five visual upgrades require
or the Governance Loop information architecture established in WI-002/WI-005
